Chapter 215: Hegemony's Monthly Revenue is 18 Million?

Shanghai.

Xin Duhui.

A group of business people were singing karaoke.

This place wasn't like Golden Age, which had extremely professional madams and an outstanding team of hostesses. But it was more exquisite and luxurious, appearing to have more class and taste.

Consequently, the "hostesses" here also seemed to have more class.

Xiong Xiaoge, the founding partner of IDG China, was showing off his near-professional level tenor voice: "...The work chants yo, echo beyond the heavens, heigh-ho, heigh-ho, floating rafts yo, delivering timber. Ten thousand high-rises are built yo, ahem-ahem-ahem-ahem yo-yo-yo-yo-yo-ho..."

*Clap clap clap clap!*

"Bravo!"

"Mr. Xiong's tenor voice is definitely at an opera singer's level."

"Haha, I bet you guys don't know. Mr. Xiong is a disciple of Mr. Wu Yanze!"

"Which Wu Yanze?"

"The one who just sang 'The Sun Never Sets on the Grassland' with A-Bao and Dai Yuqiang at the Spring Festival Gala."

Amidst a flurry of compliments, Xiong Xiaoge put down the microphone and said, "On the evenings of May 3rd, 4th, and 5th, Teacher Wu will be performing in the 'Dongfanghong Symphonic Chorus Concert.' ... Friends who are interested can go show their support."

"Definitely!"

Everyone quickly agreed.

After having some fun, Xiong Xiaoge felt his phone vibrating and excused himself to the restroom, leaving the private room.

It was a call from Lin Dongliang: "The preliminary valuation for Bailian Technology is out. There's a bit of a disagreement. Using different valuation methods, the estimate is between 300 million and 1 billion RMB!"

Xiong Xiaoge was silent for a few seconds, then commented, "A bit surprising, yet very reasonable."

"Right now, the major venture capital firms are discussing ByteDance's Series B financing plan," Lin Dongliang said. "The arguments are pretty intense. We'll probably have to increase our investment amount this time."

Xiong Xiaoge said, "Let's get the valuation for Bailian Technology sorted out first."

It was impossible to spin off Bailian Technology from ByteDance; the entire process would take several months.

ByteDance was short on funds and simply couldn't wait that long!

Why was Bailian Technology so valuable?

Because *Hegemony's* average daily peak concurrent users had reached 160,000. On weekends, it could easily break 200,000. During events, the peak concurrent users even exceeded 300,000.

With 300,000 peak concurrent users, the monthly active users could be over 1 million. Perhaps even 2 million!

Yang Yuhui's marketing team had expanded to 240 people and was frantically establishing channels in internet cafes across the nation's provincial and sub-provincial capitals.

Tao Chenggang had made his fortune by reselling IC cards, so he was no amateur when it came to promotion and distribution channels. He personally devised a set of marketing methods.

Many internet cafes didn't even need them to promote; at the request of local players, they had already installed the game.

At the same time, those internet cafe owners were proactively calling the business cooperation number on *Hegemony's* official website. Instead of waiting for top-up card resellers to stock them, they directly got a discount from Tao Chenggang, purchasing virtual top-up cards from Yunwang and Ufook, earning a commission while topping up accounts for the internet cafe's players.

*Hegemony's* monthly revenue had long surpassed that of *Legends of the Three Kingdoms*, and by a wide margin!

In February, the month of the Spring Festival, *Hegemony's* monthly revenue was over 18 million yuan. After deducting costs for administration, profit sharing, bandwidth, marketing, operations, and so on, the net profit was about 7 million yuan.

*Scions of Fate* had pretty much been beaten into submission by *Hegemony*. Active players in that game were flocking to *Hegemony*.

Only three types of people remained in *Scions of Fate*: first, those who had spent a lot of money and couldn't bear to part with their equipment; second, those who paid no attention to the outside world, just playing the game to pass the time; and third, game studios.

"Boss Tao. A whale player has appeared on the 'Jiu Jiu Lao Qin' server. His game ID is Central Plains Thug. He chose the Chu Kingdom and topped up fifty thousand on the day he joined. The next day, he topped up another twenty thousand. The third day, thirty thousand. The fourth day, another twenty thousand... As long as he's online, he always tops up at least twenty thousand!"

"He tops up that much every day? How does he spend it?" Tao Chenggang found it incredible.

"On the first day, he spent over thirty thousand just on the prize draw. He also announced in the game that he would hire people with ingots to quest with him. After the quests, they'd take him to kill monsters and run dungeons. After this person reached level 35, he started practicing life and leisure skills. To increase his cooking skill proficiency, he spent over two thousand yuan worth of ingots on materials in the auction house. He seems to have a collector's instinct, insisting on learning all the cooking recipes, and used the world chat to buy cooking recipes with ingots... These past two days, he's been opening treasure chests for fun, buying them at high prices from free-to-play players with ingots."

"Assign him a dedicated customer service representative. On call, whatever he needs."

"It's already been arranged."

Tao Chenggang considered himself worldly, but this kind of whale was still beyond his imagination.

"Boss Tao, *ZT Online* is starting its offensive again. A swarm of posts has appeared on all the major game forums, communities, and Tieba. Who knows how many paid posters they've hired!"

Tao Chenggang rushed to his computer and carefully browsed through the promotional posts for *ZT Online*.

The content of all the posts was more or less the same: *ZT Online* has been perfected, and its gameplay is richer than any other game currently available. It wasn't fun during the closed beta because it was only a half-finished product. The current perfect version is scheduled for its official open beta on World Online Game Day!

Shi Yuzhu had made a comeback.

His promotional strategy was simple and crude: hire an army of paid posters for a carpet-bombing of posts. This method was annoying, and many netizens grew tired of seeing *ZT Online* posts.

But it didn't matter.

The next day, the game channels of several major portal websites also featured *ZT Online* in the most conspicuous spots.

As the open beta date for *ZT Online* drew closer, game ads even appeared in the train stations of Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, and Shenzhen.

At the same time, a health supplement sales team totaling 2,000 people was dispatched to major cities to promote the game. They not only contacted internet cafes but also collaborated with newsstands and convenience stores on every street, ensuring that *ZT Online* top-up cards could be bought everywhere.

Tao Chenggang called Chen Guiliang and said, "That guy Shi is crazy, marketing a game like it's a health supplement!"

"I told you he would do that," Chen Guiliang said with a laugh.

Tao Chenggang said, "We haven't fully rolled out *Hegemony* in the second and third-tier cities. It's going to be troublesome with *ZT Online* snatching business like this."

"Focus on making the game experience good, retain existing players as much as possible, and then slowly attract new ones. Just pretend *ZT Online* doesn't exist!" Chen Guiliang said.

"That's easy for you to say, but... sigh!"

Tao Chenggang was very frustrated. "Shi Yuzhu got himself an exclusive interview on 17173.com yesterday. He said they printed 800,000 copies of the first batch of *ZT Online* promotional posters and plan to stick them in every corner of every internet cafe in China."

Chen Guiliang laughed loudly. "The one who should be most worried is *Scions of Fate*. With *Hegemony* in front and *ZT Online* behind, caught in a pincer attack, *Scions of Fate* will probably be forced to shut down."

Right now, there were only these three amazing free-to-play MMORPGs, plus *The Legend of Mir*.

*The Legend of Mir* had many loyal fans, *Hegemony* had seized the first-mover advantage, and *ZT Online* was just throwing insane amounts of money at it. As for *Scions of Fate*, its reputation was already ruined, and with its terrible game experience, it would probably start losing money in the next two months.

Right, there was also the recently launched *Eudemons Online*. This game was not to be underestimated either.

Chen Guiliang wasn't too concerned about *ZT Online*, nor did he even ask about the venture capital situation.

Who knew when those VCs would be able to determine Bailian Technology's valuation.

He was busy training for tug-of-war.

This weekend, Bian Guanyue came too. It wasn't entirely to hang out with Chen Guiliang; she also had her best friend, Wu Meng, at Peking University.

At this moment, Bian Guanyue and Wu Meng were sitting on the side of the sports field, chatting while watching Chen Guiliang train.

"Today we'll focus on posture first. The rest of the physical and strength training will have to be done by each team member on their own. Mainly practice squats, leg presses, lunges, pull-ups... and so on."

"As for the tug-of-war posture, let me demonstrate first..."

The university sports meet was divided into team and individual events. Tug-of-war was generally registered by department. And there had to be both men and women, with a specific limit on the number of people.

The tug-of-war team for the Yuanpei Program was mainly composed of first to third-year students.

Chen Guiliang found it quite fun. He warmed up with the other students, then learned the standard posture for gripping the rope.

"It has to be gradual, don't use all your strength at once. Let's practice pushing off the ground first... yes, just like that... then thrust your hips... your whole body leans back..."

On the side of the field.

Wu Meng, sipping bubble tea, was feeding Bian Guanyue information: "There's a girl from the Guanghua School of Management named Wan Nannan who's been getting very close to Daxia Chen recently. I have a mole in the Yuanpei Program, you know. According to my informant, Wan Nannan often saves seats for Daxia Chen!"

"Is she pretty?" Bian Guanyue asked.

Wu Meng said, "She's alright. But nowhere near as pretty as you."

Bian Guanyue smiled. "Then it's fine."

She was getting to know Chen Guiliang better and better.

When Chen Guiliang dealt with women, he first looked at their appearance, and second, he was afraid of trouble.

If a woman who wasn't exceptionally beautiful pursued him, Chen Guiliang would definitely refuse just to avoid trouble. He didn't have the time to waste on entanglements; he'd rather use that time to catch up on sleep.

Bian Guanyue changed the subject. "I planted two trees on Arbor Day."

"You certainly have the leisure for that," Wu Meng laughed.

Bian Guanyue said, "I joined the school's volunteer association. When the 2008 Olympics come, I can represent the school as an Olympic volunteer. This tree planting was also organized by the volunteer association."

"What exactly do Olympic volunteers do?" Wu Meng asked curiously.

Bian Guanyue said, "I'm not exactly sure, but there will be a lot of things to do."

Wu Meng thought for a moment. "By the 2008 Olympics, we'll have graduated, won't we?"

"You can still be a volunteer after graduating," Bian Guanyue said. "When the time comes, I'll also buy tickets to watch the games and cheer for Liu Xiang and the others in person!"

An hour of training passed in a flash.

"Chen Guiliang, aren't you staying to practice squats?"

"I ride my bike every day."

Chen Guiliang ran over to get his bicycle. "Where are you two beauties off to today?"

"The Summer Palace. Guanguan and I have already decided," Wu Meng said.

"Hop on!"

This old Phoenix-brand bicycle could carry two women.

Wu Meng was more petite, so she sat on the crossbar. Bian Guanyue sat on the rear rack.

Chen Guiliang pedaled hard, beauties both in front of and behind him. He suddenly began to fantasize: if Tao Xue were on the crossbar and Bian Guanyue were still on the back, that would surely feel wonderful.

The prerequisite was that they got along harmoniously—which was a bit difficult.

Tao Xue's college entrance exams were in a few months, and she had made it clear she was coming to Beijing. Just thinking about it now gave Chen Guiliang a headache.

He'd just have to take it one step at a time.

(End of this chapter)
